newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, bearish tone prevails.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, bearish tone prevails.

text.p: Gold prices were balanced on recent lows on Monday with dealers expecting further weakness before a floor could be established.
"There has been some two-way business this morning but it is still under pressure and there could be more room on the downside," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $343.75 per ounce after $345.50 on Friday and a close then of $344.35/$344.85.
Prices, which had been hovering uneasily around the mid $350s until the middle of last week, weakened on renewed rumours of a central bank sale.
The market came under pressure also from what some dealers said was producer selling towards the end of last week.
Fresh buying was sparse on Monday as the bearish tone in the market continued.

"People are still very wary about the central bank rumour and the dollar is too strong to tempt buyers into gold," a dealer said, adding that the dollar's strength was bringing some selling of metal out of South Africa.
Some dealers noted that physical buying had picked up in Dubai partly for on-carriage to India and that the end of Ramadan this week could help sustain physical interest.
Countering that, Hong Kong closes tomorrow until February 10 for the Lunar New Year holiday.
But the physical business would not be sufficient to turn the market, dealers said.
"There is too much hanging over it at the moment. Speculators are just not willing to stick a toe in yet," a dealer said.
Silver was indicated at $4.86/$4.88 down four cents from Friday's close and towards the lower end of a $4.80-$5.05 range traced last week.
"Silver suffered along with gold on the central bank rumours but physical demand has been very good," a dealer said.
There was a risk of prices coming off if physical offtake was not sustained , the dealer added.
Silver was largely the beneficiary of ratio plays against gold last week which took it through resistances in the $4.90s.
But now that it was under $4.90 and with gold weaker as well, it could be vulnerable to pressure, dealers said.
Palladium fixed at its highest level since September 9, 1996 at $124.30, 65 cents ahead of Friday, after Japanese consumers bought in Tokyo earlier in the day.
Talks to settle Russian supplies to Japan for 1997 have been delayed which has encouraged consumer and speculator buying of the metal.
Platinum was struggling around recent lows and was indicated at $348.50/$349.50, just 25 cents above its Friday close.
